title: Competitive market equilibrium
summary: Demand and supply set the equilibrium price. Prices signal and give incentives, rationing scarce goods. At equilibrium, social surplus is maximised. HL calculates equilibrium from functions.

keyterms.definition: The price and quantity at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied, so there is no tendency to change.
When quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price, putting upward pressure on price.
When quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded at the current price, putting downward pressure on price.
The way prices adjust to changes in demand and supply to allocate scarce resources.
Price changes give information to buyers and sellers about where resources are wanted.
Price changes motivate producers and consumers to change their behaviour, e.g. higher prices encourage more output.
Higher prices limit who buys a scarce good to those most willing and able to pay.
The difference between the maximum price consumers are willing to pay and the price they actually pay.
The difference between the price producers receive and the minimum price they would accept.
Consumer surplus plus producer surplus; maximised at the competitive equilibrium when there are no market failures.
Producing the combination of goods society values most; occurs where marginal benefit equals marginal cost (MSB = MSC).
Setting Qd = Qs to find the equilibrium price, then substituting back to find equilibrium quantity.

questions.prompt: At a price above equilibrium, what exists and what happens next?
options: Excess demand; price tends to rise
Excess supply; price tends to rise
Excess supply; price tends to fall
questions.explanation: Above equilibrium, Qs > Qd; sellers cut prices to clear unsold stock.

questions.statement: At a price below equilibrium there is a shortage, which pushes price up.
questions.explanation: Qd > Qs; buyers compete for the limited supply and price rises towards equilibrium.

questions.prompt: Demand for electric bikes rises. Which price function makes producers switch resources into making e-bikes?
questions.explanation: Higher prices and profits create an incentive for firms to produce more.

questions.text: Demand rises while supply is unchanged: equilibrium price ___ and quantity rises.
questions.explanation: A rightward demand shift moves along the supply curve to a higher price and quantity.

questions.prompt: Supply increases AND demand increases at the same time. What is certain?
questions.explanation: Both shifts raise quantity; the price effect depends on which shift is larger.

questions.prompt: Match each market change to the effect on equilibrium.
questions.explanation: Use a diagram: shift the curve and read off the new intersection.

questions.statement: Higher concert ticket prices that leave only the most willing fans buying show the rationing function of price.
questions.explanation: Price rations scarce goods to those willing and able to pay most.

questions.text: The way prices adjust to allocate scarce resources is called the price ___.
questions.explanation: Adam Smith’s "invisible hand" describes this decentralised allocation.

questions.prompt: Order the adjustment after a frost destroys half the orange crop.
items: A shortage appears at the old price
Higher price signals farmers to expand future output
questions.explanation: The price mechanism rations and signals in response to the supply shock.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the price mechanism is accurate?
options: It always gives a fair distribution of income
It coordinates millions of decisions without central planning
It works only when government sets prices
It cannot respond to changes in tastes
questions.explanation: Prices coordinate decentralised decisions efficiently, but say nothing about equity.

lessons.title: Consumer surplus, producer surplus and efficiency

questions.prompt: A consumer would pay up to $50 for a jacket and buys it for $35. What is her consumer surplus?
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus = willingness to pay − price paid = 50 − 35 = $15.

questions.statement: Producer surplus is the area above the supply curve and below the price.
questions.explanation: It shows the gain to producers from selling at a price above their minimum acceptable price.

questions.text: Consumer surplus plus producer surplus equals ___ surplus.
questions.explanation: Social (community) surplus is maximised at the competitive equilibrium without externalities.

options: marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost
questions.explanation: MSB = MSC means society cannot gain by producing more or less.

questions.statement: Any price above the competitive equilibrium raises social surplus.
questions.explanation: Moving away from equilibrium creates a deadweight (welfare) loss and reduces social surplus.

questions.prompt: A consumer would pay up to $8 for a sandwich, and the sandwich costs the seller $3 to make. It sells for $5. What is the social surplus from this sale?
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus = 8 − 5 = $3 and producer surplus = 5 − 3 = $2, so social surplus = $5.

questions.text: At the competitive equilibrium without externalities, marginal benefit equals marginal cost, so resources are allocated ___.
questions.explanation: MB = MC at equilibrium means allocative efficiency and maximum social surplus.

questions.prompt: Match each area on a demand and supply diagram to its name.

pairs.left: Area below demand and above price
Area above supply and below price

questions.explanation: Social surplus is greatest at the competitive equilibrium.

lessons.title: HL: Calculating equilibrium from linear functions

questions.prompt: HL: Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = −20 + 4P. What is the equilibrium price?
HL: Using the same functions (Qd = 100 − 2P, Qs = −20 + 4P), what is equilibrium quantity?
questions.explanation: Substitute P = 20: Qd = 100 − 40 = 60 (check: Qs = −20 + 80 = 60).

questions.text: HL: With Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = −20 + 4P, at P = 15 there is excess demand of ___ units.
questions.explanation: Qd = 70, Qs = 40, so excess demand = 30.

questions.prompt: HL: Qd = 100 − 2P, Qs = −20 + 4P. Match each price to the market situation.
questions.explanation: At P = 25, Qd = 50 and Qs = 80. At P = 5, Qs = 0.

questions.prompt: HL: Order the steps to find equilibrium from linear functions.
questions.explanation: Solving the simultaneous equations gives the price where plans match.

questions.prompt: HL: Qd = 90 − 3P and Qs = −10 + 2P. What is the equilibrium price?

questions.statement: HL: If Qd = 90 − 3P and Qs = −10 + 2P, there is excess supply at a price of 25.
questions.explanation: At P = 25, Qd = 15 and Qs = 40, so excess supply = 25 units.

questions.text: HL: Qd = 100 − 2P and Qs = −20 + 4P. Demand rises to Qd = 130 − 2P. The new equilibrium price is ___.
